After lunch, guidance on waiting areas
This section sets out the main rule first, then the reasons
Companion Animal Travel Desk Waiting Area Care

The Companion Animal Travel Desk is responsible for calm, clean, and supervised waiting areas that place animal welfare ahead of convenience. Staff must guide travelers to the right seating, keep passages clear, and watch for signs of stress, illness, or unsafe handling. Leila Moretti and Nora Suleiman may receive support here when traveling with pets, and Simba may be offered extra space when needed. All care choices must favor safety over speed, with the senior coordinator making the final daily service decision when guidance is needed.

Staff must keep carriers secure, prevent mingling that could unsettle animals, and offer water or relief support when it is safe to do so. <<FACT F027>> Any pet placed in a waiting area must be observed with care, and concerns about containment, noise, or separation should be raised at once.

The pet lounge, where available, must remain welcoming, orderly, and easy to supervise. <<FACT F006>> Staff should use gentle language, respect animal temperaments, and respond promptly to signs of distress so that travelers feel supported rather than hurried.

When a hazard is found, the safety coordinator must be informed without delay, and the senior coordinator should review any change in handling or routing before the animal moves onward. If a traveler needs further assistance, contact the senior coordinator or the safety coordinator through the Companion Animal Travel Desk.
